title: A titanic interstellar medium ejection from a massive starburst galaxy at redshift 1.4
question: What is the physical mechanism driving a massive molecular gas ejection event in the starburst galaxy ID2299 at z = 1.4, and what is its impact on star formation quenching?

what.value: Rest-frame 2-10 keV absorption-corrected X-ray luminosity L_X-ray ~ 1.6 x 10^43 erg s^-1

evidence.loc: A disruptive event in a massive galaxy at z=1.4
evidence.quote: The object is detected in the X-rays and has a weak rest-frame 2-10 keV absorption-corrected luminosity(cite: Civano16) L$_{\rm X-ray} \sim 1.6 \times 10^{43} \ {\rm erg s^{-1}}$

what.value: SuperDeblended far-IR/(sub)-millimetre catalog and UV-to-far-IR broad-band photometry in COSMOS

evidence.quote: We measure L$_{\rm FIR}$ by fitting the SuperDeblended far-IR/(sub)-millimetre catalog in COSMOS(cite: Jin18) using the procedure described in a previous paper(cite: Jin18).
We derive these quantities through multi-wavelength spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting to the COSMOS broad-band photometry from the UV to the far-IR (cite: Laigle16; Jin18)

what.value: 1.4-3 GHz radio luminosity and VLBA 1.4 GHz 3sigma upper limit log(L_radio / W Hz^-1) <= 23.55

evidence.quote: However, the 1.4-3 GHz radio luminosity of ID2299 is fully accounted by star formation (cite: Delvecchio17). Deep VLBA 1.4 GHz observations(cite: HerreraRuiz17) at $0.01''$ resolution sampling circumnuclear scales (85 pc at z=1.4) where the core AGN jet is supposed to be launched, give a 3$\sigma$ upper limit log(L$_{\rm radio}/{\rm W\ Hz^{-1}}) \leq 23.55$.

recipe.goal: Measure stellar mass, SFR, and AGN bolometric luminosity via SED fitting
recipe.method: Fit multi-wavelength UV to far-IR photometry from COSMOS and the SuperDeblended catalog using CIGALE and far-IR SED fitting, cleaning L_FIR from AGN contribution
key_parameters: FIR integration range lambda in [8 - 1000] um
assumptions: Chabrier (2003) IMF, dividing Kennicutt (1998) conversion by a factor 1.7

recipe.goal: Classify morphology and measure optical/NIR size
recipe.method: Visual and quantitative morphological analysis (Shape asymmetry, Gini, M20) on HST F814W image, and 2D profile fitting on Ks-band image using GALFIT
key_parameters: Shape asymmetry minimum threshold for merger = 0.2

recipe.goal: Measure sub-millimetre source size in the uv plane
recipe.method: Extract signal amplitude vs uv distance from each ALMA tracer using GILDAS scripts, scale uv-distances to a common frequency, marginalize over normalization, and fit circular Gaussian models

recipe.goal: Extract 1D spectra, subtract continuum, and fit narrow and broad emission lines
recipe.method: Extract ALMA spectra in uv space using a Gaussian model of radius R_eff,ALMA = 1.54 kpc, subtract a power-law continuum, and fit narrow + broad Gaussian components with MPFIT in ALMA and DEIMOS [OII] spectra
key_parameters: Continuum power-law slope = 3.7 with nu_0 = 101.25, 248.40, 342.55 GHz; CO(5-4), [CI](2-1), CO(7-6) broad centroid and width tied to CO(2-1); [OII] flux ratio I_3729/I_3726 = 1.5
assumptions: Source extension modeled as a Gaussian of radius R_eff,ALMA = 1.54 kpc; low-density limit for [OII] doublet ratio

recipe.goal: Image the broad component in the ALMA cubes
recipe.method: Subtract best-fit 1D continuum and narrow-line model at each frequency in the uv plane using GILDAS UVFIT within R_eff,ALMA, and recombine residuals into a cube
key_parameters: Subtraction performed within R_eff,ALMA = 1.54 kpc over full frequency range of the spectral window

recipe.goal: Compute molecular and ionized gas masses, mass outflow rates, and broad-component SFR
recipe.method: Convert CO(2-1) luminosities to molecular gas masses, [OII] luminosity to ionized gas mass using IRAF TEMDEN emissivity, CO(5-4) broad luminosity to SFR_broad, and calculate outflow rates under spherical/conical geometry
key_parameters: R_OF = R_eff,ALMA = 1.54 kpc; v_max = (v_broad - v_narrow) + 2*sigma_broad = 634 km s^-1 (or v_mol,b = 179 km s^-1 for conservative tidal scenario)
assumptions: L'_CO(2-1)/L'_CO(1-0) = 0.85 and alpha_CO = 0.8 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1
Ionized gas T_e = 10^4 K, n_e = 300 cm^-3, solar metallicity, no dust attenuation correction

recipe.goal: Test two-galaxy merger hypothesis via dynamical mass
recipe.method: Compute dynamical mass of the broad component using a merger-calibrated thin-disk rotator formula and compare with rescaled stellar + molecular mass within the ALMA area
key_parameters: f_c = 10^0.45 = 2.81; inclination i = 57 deg; R_eff,ALMA = 1.54 kpc; v_FWHM,mol,b = 535 km s^-1
assumptions: Thin-disk rotator with merger correction factor f_c = 2.81, average random inclination i = 57 deg, negligible dark matter within 1.54 kpc, and 50% stellar mass split between the two putative galaxies

recipe.goal: Model molecular gas excitation (CO + [CI] SLED) with LVG models
recipe.method: Normalize narrow and broad line flux densities to CO(2-1) = 1 and fit two-component Large Velocity Gradient (LVG) models using MICHI2

recipe.goal: Compute cosmic rate of disruptive events
recipe.method: Divide the completeness-corrected number of detected disruptive events in the survey comoving volume by the typical event duration and compare with starburst merger density
key_parameters: 1 event out of 35 starbursts (123 galaxies total); completeness correction = 7% of starbursts at 1.1 <= z <= 1.7; t_disr = 5 +/- 1 Myr; survey volume = 10^7 Mpc^3; 25% fraction of starbursts ejecting large tails; t_dyn,merger = 100 Myr
assumptions: Starbursts defined as SFR >= 4 x SFR_MS; 20-30% of starbursts eject large gas tails with visibility window 50-200 Myr

answer_key.quantity: Broad CO(7-6) integrated flux upper limit (I_CO(7-6),b)

evidence.quote: Here we present a massive starburst galaxy at $z=1.4$ which is ejecting $46 \pm 13$% of its molecular gas mass at a startling rate of $\gtrsim 10,000$ M$_{\odot}{\rm yr}^{-1}$.

Assuming that the gas in the broad component is associated to a feedback-driven wind (e.g., from AGN or star-formation), would translate its gas mass into an exceptional mass outflow rate $\dot{\rm M}_{\rm mol, OF} = 25000 \ \pm \ 8000$ M$_{\odot}{\rm yr}^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Molecular mass outflow rate (tidal ejection / average velocity shift)

evidence.quote: (t$_{\rm OF} \sim 10$ Myr and $\dot{\rm M}_{\rm mol, OF} = 7100 \ \pm \ 3600$ M$_{\odot}{\rm yr}^{-1}$, if one were instead to use the most conservative average velocity shift v$_{\rm mol, b} = 179 \ {\rm km s^{-1}}$ ).
This corresponds to a mass outflow rate $\dot{\rm M}_{\rm OF, ion} = \ 20 \pm$ 7 M$_{\odot}$yr$^{-1}$.
this computation assumes that the outflow has a velocity v$_{\rm max, OF} = 634 \pm 139 \ {\rm km s^{-1}}$ and extends over R$_{\rm OF} = 1.54 \pm 0.04$ kpc

answer_key.quantity: Star formation rate in broad component (SFR_broad)

evidence.loc: Triggering mechanism of the disruptive event
evidence.quote: From the luminosity of the broad CO(5-4) component, we estimate that the ejected material is forming stars at a rate of SFR$_{\rm broad} = 180 \pm 60$ M$_{\odot} {\rm yr}^{-1}$.

evidence.loc: Frequency of disruptive events and connection with the quenched galaxy population
evidence.quote: This single event was extracted from a survey of 123 objects and thus implies $\sim (1 - 2) \times 10^4 {\rm /Mpc^3/Gyr}$ disruptive events per cosmic volume and unit time (Figure 3, see Methods). The error associated to this measurement is $\sim 0.6 \ {\rm dex}$
The continuum underlying the CO(2-1) emission is almost undetected (SNR $\sim$ 2, S$_{0} = 0.05 \pm 0.02 \ {\rm mJy}$).
Instead, we detect a strong continuum under the CO(5-4) emission (SNR $\sim$ 14, S$_0 = 1.80 \pm 0.12  \ {\rm mJy}$)
and below the \[CI\](2-1)+CO(7-6) emission (SNR $\gtrsim 100$, S$_{0} = 5.04 \pm 0.15 \ {\rm mJy}$).

answer_key.quantity: Low-excitation H2 density in narrow component (log n_H2)

evidence.loc: Molecular gas conditions of the galaxy and of the ejected material
evidence.quote: The low-excitation component of this gas has a density log(n$_{\rm H2}/{\rm cm}^{-3}) = 2.9 \pm 0.8$ whereas the high-excitation component has log(n$_{\rm H2}/{\rm cm}^{-3}) = 5.2 \pm 1.2$.

answer_key.quantity: High-excitation H2 density in narrow component (log n_H2)

evidence.loc: Molecular gas conditions of the galaxy and of the ejected material
evidence.quote: The low-excitation component of this gas has a density log(n$_{\rm H2}/{\rm cm}^{-3}) = 2.9 \pm 0.8$ whereas the high-excitation component has log(n$_{\rm H2}/{\rm cm}^{-3}) = 5.2 \pm 1.2$.

answer_key.quantity: Low-density H2 in broad component (log n_H2)

evidence.loc: Molecular gas conditions of the galaxy and of the ejected material
evidence.quote: We find evidence of the presence of ISM-like low- and high-density gas having log(n$_{\rm H2}/{\rm cm}^{-3}) = 2.7 \pm 0.7$ and log(n$_{\rm H2}/{\rm cm}^{-3}) = 4.55 \pm 1.85$ respectively.

answer_key.quantity: High-density H2 in broad component (log n_H2)

evidence.loc: Molecular gas conditions of the galaxy and of the ejected material
evidence.quote: We find evidence of the presence of ISM-like low- and high-density gas having log(n$_{\rm H2}/{\rm cm}^{-3}) = 2.7 \pm 0.7$ and log(n$_{\rm H2}/{\rm cm}^{-3}) = 4.55 \pm 1.85$ respectively.
